summary: 本文だけを文脈非継承で点検し、3件の問題候補を検出した。発音の地域差表記、criteria単数用法のスコープ、語源上の関連語の関係強度を修正後に再確認する。

findings.description: The kana approximation is presented as one English flow even though the preceding IPA distinguishes the US /tɪr/ and UK /tɪə/ nuclei.
findings.reason: A learner could treat クライ・ティア・リアン as the only pronunciation and miss the US rhotic vowel/consonant sequence.
findings.suggested_direction: State the US and UK kana approximations separately, or qualify the current approximation as mainly UK-like.

scope_anchors.exact_quote: 語頭は cry と同じ /kraɪ/ で、語末は /iən/ と続くため、英語では「クライ・ティア・リアン」に近い音の流れになる。

findings.location: ＃意味・用法・関連表現 line:73
findings.description: The note on singular criteria narrows the growing singular use to conversation or casual writing without stating that it is a broader current-English usage under formal dispute.
findings.reason: The scope may teach learners that singular criteria is only colloquial, while the actual usage issue is current but contested and formal-style dependent.
findings.suggested_direction: Remove the conversation-only framing; say singular criteria is increasingly used in current English, while criterion remains the safer choice in formal standard writing.

scope_anchors.exact_quote: criteria を単数として a criteria・criteria is とする用法も、特に会話やくだけた文章では広がっているが、学習者が標準的な書き言葉で使う場合は criterion を選ぶ。

findings.description: The related-word sentence groups critic, critical, and crisis as one Greek-root family and may be read as a direct derivational relation from criterion.
findings.reason: The paragraph needs a clearer distinction between a broad etymological root family and direct word formation; otherwise the learner may infer a stronger lexical relation than intended.
findings.suggested_direction: Qualify these as etymologically related root-family examples and state that they are not direct derivatives or synonyms; remove any member that cannot be supported at that scope.

scope_anchors.exact_quote: 同じ語根の語として、critic「批評家、批評する人」、critical「批評の、重大な」や crisis「危機、重大な転機」がある。
